big_idea: Events are IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, or CERTAIN. We predict using likelihood.
learning_intention: We are learning to use likelihood vocabulary.
success_criteria: I can name an event IMPOSSIBLE.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Lucky and Mae — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Lucky: WILL it snow today? Sometimes! Will the sun come up tomorrow? CERTAIN! Will I fly to the moon? IMPOSSIBLE! Lucky opens: 'NEVER, ALWAYS, or SOMETIMES?' Class: 'I, C, or P!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Lucky and Mae puppets. 'Friends — last year you learned likelihood. Today we REVIEW.'

Review vocabulary. Write IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN on chart. 'Impossible = NEVER. Possible = MAYBE. Certain = ALWAYS.'

Demo. Hold up event cards. 'Snow in July → IMPOSSIBLE. Rain at recess → POSSIBLE. Day will end → CERTAIN.'

More Canadian examples:
- 'Maple syrup tastes sweet' → CERTAIN.
- 'Snow in May' → POSSIBLE (sometimes).
- 'Pigs play hockey' → IMPOSSIBLE.
- 'Sunny tomorrow' → POSSIBLE.
- 'Polar bear in our class' → IMPOSSIBLE.
- 'Lunch happens today' → CERTAIN.

'Lucky says — every event fits ONE of three. Decide.'

'Today we sort lots of events. We'll add a NEW idea tomorrow: complementary events.'

Introduce PREDICT. 'Predict = use likelihood to say what will happen.'

Demo prediction: 'Will it be sunny tomorrow? POSSIBLE. I predict — yes!' Or no.

'Today YOU predict events.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: name 6 events as I/P/C with Canadian context.
Three stations. A: Sort 12 cards. B: Predict 5 events. C: Make own events.
Stretch at C: justify each likelihood.

STRATEGY COMPARE: Two children share contrasting events for the same category. Class votes on which is 'more impossible' or 'more certain' and JUSTIFIES with cause-effect reasoning (Jones et al. 1997 Level 2).
steps.teacher_prompt: Lucky: 'Same category, different EVIDENCE. Probability is about REASONS.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children move to 3 corners by likelihood.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: names I, P, C.

consolidation.exit_routine: Lucky's refrain — class chants: Lucky calls 'NEVER, ALWAYS, or SOMETIMES?' Class chants 'I, C, or P!' (Impossible, Certain, Possible). Repeat 3x. Each child writes one event + tag on a sticky.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says POSSIBLE for everything — repairing the all-possible default at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On 'name likelihood as IMPOSSIBLE / POSSIBLE / CERTAIN', Grade-2 children frequently classify everything as POSSIBLE because 'anything could happen.' Fischbein (1975, 'The Intuitive Sources of Probabilistic Thinking in Children') and Jones, Langrall, Thornton & Mogill (1997 framework) place the move from 'anything is possible' to ordered IMPOSSIBLE/POSSIBLE/CERTAIN as the gateway of probabilistic reasoning. Without it, Lessons 2-5 cannot ground.

Today reviews the 3 categories. Tomorrow Lesson 2 introduces complementary events; Lesson 3 spinners; Lesson 4 dice; Lesson 5 mode prediction capstone.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair at Station A. Card: 'A snowman in our class.' Child says POSSIBLE.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said POSSIBLE. But Lucky asks — could a real snowman BE in our class right now? Snowmen melt. So it's IMPOSSIBLE.'

Guide. 'IMPOSSIBLE = never (snowman in classroom). CERTAIN = always (sun rises). POSSIBLE = maybe (rain).'

Generlise. 'Lucky says — ask: NEVER, ALWAYS, or SOMETIMES?'
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child sorts everything as POSSIBLE: anchor with obviously-impossible ('a fish flies to the moon') and obviously-certain ('we breathe air'); child anchors before tackling middle cases.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can name TRUE/FALSE but not likelihood: drill the must-happen test 'is it locked-in or just LIKELY?' — locked = CERTAIN, otherwise POSSIBLE.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child swaps IMPOSSIBLE and POSSIBLE: physical sorting hoop — IMPOSSIBLE cards never touch the centre POSSIBLE hoop. Spatial separation prevents accidents.

parts_outline.task: Sort 6 events as I, P, or C.
Write your own event for each category.
